R696.note: jwt.verify with an explicit algorithms list and try/catch closes the forged-token path; the newly required JWT_SECRET and the 401-on-invalid path are inherent to verification and are stated plainly.

R697.note: Dropping the envp array closes the env-injection sink, but the fix also routes param into argv as a new command argument (regex allows a leading '-', so option injection is unguarded), replaces Runtime.exec's environment replacement with inherited env silently, and rejects previously-accepted header values with an uncaught IllegalArgumentException.

R698.note: fast-xml-parser with processEntities:false is a sound XXE close, but processEntities:false also stops decoding predefined entities (& etc.) and the pure-JS parser no longer errors on malformed XML that libxmljs rejected - neither stated, and //order/id at any depth becomes a root-only lookup.

R699.note: Re-indexing tasks[activeIndex] after the push_back removes the invalidated reference with identical observable semantics.

R700.note: SigningMethodHMAC assertion in keyFunc plus WithValidMethods pins the algorithm server-side; the HS256 pin is the standard shape and is stated, and the write-up's ordering claim (validMethods checked before keyFunc) matches golang-jwt v5.

R701.note: Strict in_array allowlist before require closes the traversal, but the three permitted names are invented with no evidence of what lives in plugins/, so a real approved plugin outside the guessed list now throws - and the write-up does not flag the list as needing to be filled from the actual directory.

R702.note: Deletion moved to POST behind protection.Handler with the GET route kept as a confirmation form; the extra confirmation step for email links is stated and legitimate deletion still succeeds.

R703.note: Path.resolve() plus is_relative_to closes the symlink escape while nested paths, absolute/escaping paths and download_name behave as before; the write-up's claim that strict=True prevents TOCTTOU is wrong but the code is unaffected.

R704.note: Splitting the argument only closes the POSIX branch (confirmed by running: 'sh -c echo <param>' makes param $0, unprinted and unevaluated) - the Windows branch still feeds param unquoted onto cmd.exe /c, where ProcessBuilder quotes only space/tab/</>, so & | ^ still inject; and the fix silently turns the echo output into an empty line while the explanation claims param is echoed literally.

R705.note: Per-stream setObjectInputFilter with an allowlist ending in !* keeps the native wire format and the RuntimeException path intact, exactly the contract's shape; the 8u121 attribution is loose (java.io.ObjectInputFilter is 9+) but the code is right.

R706.note: AES/GCM/NoPadding with a fresh SecureRandom 12-byte IV replaces ECB; the response stays Base64 and the IV-prepended layout needed for decryption is stated explicitly.

R707.note: Rejecting when bytesRead < 8 does stop the comparison running over unfilled buffer bytes, but the right shape here is ReadExactly/a read loop - a legitimate large upload whose first Read returns short now gets a 400 labelled 'File is too short', a consequence the write-up does not draw despite naming the mechanism.

R708.note: Escaping the parens, asterisk and backslash closes the filter injection, but the escaper also maps a space to the NUL escape sequence (backslash-zero-zero, not a space escape) while the write-up describes that branch as escaping the NULL character, so any legitimate value containing a space is silently rewritten to contain a NUL and stops matching.
